small_guidance:
- Try larger BLOCK_HW (512 or 1024) with BLOCK_IC=64 to better amortize the inner KH*KW loop and reduce w_tile reloads; also try BLOCK_OC=128 with num_warps=8.
- Hoist the weight tile load out of the hw_start loop — weights `w[ic, oc, kh, kw]` do not depend on `hw_start`, so currently they are reloaded HW/BLOCK_HW times per (ic_start, kh, kw). Load all KH*KW weight tiles once per ic_start and reuse across the HW loop.
- Add a `triton.autotune` over BLOCK_HW∈{256,512,1024}, BLOCK_IC∈{16,32,64}, BLOCK_OC∈{32,64,128}, num_warps∈{4,8}, num_stages∈{2,3,4}.
large_guidance:
- Swap the loop order: outer loop over IC (load weight tile [BLOCK_IC, BLOCK_OC, KH, KW] once), middle over KH/KW (static), inner over HW; this keeps weights in registers and only streams x. Currently weights are re-fetched for every HW tile.
- Note that mean over the OH×OW output grid of a ConvTranspose2d is equivalent to a weighted sum over input positions where the weight per (ic, oc, ih, iw) is Σ_{kh,kw} 1[oh,ow in bounds] · w[ic,oc,kh,kw]/(OH·OW). Doing this fusion correctly still requires iterating the full (ih,iw,kh,kw) space per output element (no axis collapsed in weight space pre-runtime), but lets us avoid materializing OH·OW outputs. Make sure the kernel iterates the full input H·W × KH·KW work (it does), and consider one program per (N, OC-tile) doing a single GEMM-like reduction of shape (IC·KH·KW) × (H·W) into BLOCK_OC accumulators using tl.dot.
- Persistent kernel: with N=16 and OC=128, launch grid (N, OC/BLOCK_OC) and use tl.dot on a [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_IC] × [BLOCK_IC, BLOCK_HW] tile, accumulating into [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_HW] then reducing along HW at the end for true tensor-core utilization.
